g.text: 1 · Rebuild exactly the SQL the dashboard runs on page 1
page1_queries() rebuilds the dashboard JSON with the same builder and turns every page-1 widget query into SELECT <fields> FROM (<dataset>) t GROUP BY <fields> (bench.py:46-62),
including the 16 filter-dropdown queries. Dashboard parameters are inlined with their default values (literal_sql, bench.py:31-43). Baseline: 28 queries.
2 · Warm the warehouse before anything is timed
SELECT 1 to make sure the warehouse is running, then one full page load without result cache that is not recorded (bench.py:116-118).
So 'first load' = warm warehouse and disk cache, no result cache. The replay does not invalidate tables.
3 · One session per query, opened before the clock starts
run_page() opens one databricks-sql-connector session per query, in parallel, before the timer starts (bench.py:82-85),
with use_cached_result=false (first load) or true (subsequent load) as session configuration (bench.py:65-71).
4 · Page time = t0 → the last of the 28 parallel queries has returned all rows
t0 = perf_counter(), then 28 threads fire all queries at once. Each thread times its own execute() + fetchall() (bench.py:74-79).
Page time = until the thread pool is done, i.e. the slowest query has returned all rows (bench.py:86-90). Example: slowest query 8.95 s → page 9.17 s.
5 · 10 runs without result cache, one priming run, 10 runs with result cache
10 × run_page(cache=False) = first loads, 1 priming run with cache on (not recorded), 10 × run_page(cache=True) = subsequent loads (bench.py:119-130).
Per-query times are kept for the first-load runs. The slowest query per run is printed to the log.
6 · Write the result file and combine it with the browser numbers
The runner writes results/replay_<variant>_<warehouse>.json itself: raw run times, mean / median / stdev and per-query times (bench.py:132-150).
report.py:38 loads it next to the browser runs for the result tables.
